svg.text: Test setup for step 3. Only the laptop USB is needed: the Nucleo 5V pin feeds the top + rail (5 V).
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
outside the board, facing the dog,
joined with 4 female to male wires
Column map of the whole feeder:
5 V: Nucleo 5V to the top + rail; sensor VCC
ECHO from the sensor (5 V signal)
ECHO to Nucleo D9 · PD15 (3.3 V, after the divider)
Echo gives 5 V; an STM32 pin wants 3.3 V.
1 kΩ from Echo to PD15, 2 kΩ from PD15 to GND:
Bands: 1 kΩ brown black red, 2 kΩ red black red.
Trig needs no resistor: 3.3 V starts the sensor.
1. Wire everything with the USB unplugged.
2. VCC on 5 V: the HC-SR04 does not work on 3.3 V.
3. Never connect Echo straight to the Nucleo.
4. Keep the front clear (range 2 cm to 4 m).
5. Feeder: an animal under 40 cm starts a photo.
6. Check every Nucleo pin label before plugging.
Kibbly hardware · circuit 3 of the circuits by part · wires U1 to U8 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 8, rails R1, R3 and R4 in section 4B
